findings.claim: Valid modifiers outside the reader's list are now reported as compiler errors with spelling advice. In the real page `private transient int current = 18;` gives "Error, line 5: <identifier> expected. Java expected a name here: check the spelling of the words on line 5." and `private synchronized int clamp(int t)` gives the same on line 16; javac accepts both (volatile, native and strictfp are in the same position). The new repeated-modifier advice is also wrong for a non-access modifier: `private final final int target` gives "repeated modifier. Keep at most one access modifier (public, protected or private)", though final is not an access modifier. Not a try and unlikely on this task, hence low, but this is the access-modifiers page and the editor now speaks with compiler authority about modifiers.

evidence.section: JLS SE 25 8.3.1 Field Modifiers (FieldModifier grammar includes transient and volatile)
JLS SE 25 8.4.3 Method Modifiers (MethodModifier grammar includes synchronized, native and strictfp)

findings.recommendation: Add transient, volatile, synchronized, native and strictfp to MODS (or report them as not supported, never as a compiler error), and make the repeated-modifier advice say "Write each modifier only once on line N".
